chapters.title: THE FVNNY STOIC
chapters.tease: The feed is the first text in human history built never to finish. You, unfortunately, are not.

chapters.title: The Infinite Scroll
chapters.tease: A two-thousand-year-old sorting algorithm meets your timeline, and the old code still runs perfectly.

chapters.title: The Dichotomy, Updated
chapters.tease: Check your phone before you make anything, and strangers write the first paragraph of your day.

chapters.title: The Morning Gate
chapters.tease: Your anger now has a global supply chain, a quality-control team and quarterly earnings. Who exactly is profiting?

chapters.title: Outrage as a Service
chapters.tease: Your online enemies have been cast, costumed and delivered by an algorithm with excellent taste in what enrages you.

chapters.title: The Curated Enemy
chapters.tease: Forecast tomorrow's annoyances tonight, by name, and they arrive as appointments instead of ambushes.

chapters.title: Premeditatio, Notification Edition
chapters.tease: Muting is not cowardice. A library refuses more books than it shelves and nobody calls it fragile.

chapters.title: The Mute Is Mightier
chapters.tease: The doomscroll is a closed loop with exactly one power source, and it is holding your phone.

chapters.title: The Doomscroll Ouroboros
chapters.tease: Marcus Aurelius had the reach of the known world, and chose to write for an audience of one.

chapters.title: What the Stoics Would Have Posted
chapters.tease: The feed is not defeated by insight. It is defeated by one small click, repeated every night.

chapters.title: The Closed Tab
chapters.tease: Your envy was built for a village of 150 people. The feed now runs it against eight billion.

chapters.title: Comparison at Scale
chapters.tease: Everyone else's life looks better because you are comparing their trailer with your full, unedited footage.

chapters.title: The Highlight Reel Fallacy
chapters.tease: Comparison is the thief of joy. Theodore Roosevelt never said it, and it is true anyway.

chapters.title: The Thief
chapters.tease: Why does enough always move as you approach it? Because you drew the line in pencil.

chapters.title: Enough
chapters.tease: Count the people who would help you carry a sofa downstairs. That is your only follower count with a load rating.

chapters.title: The Follower Fallacy
chapters.tease: You have been entered into dozens of competitions you never signed up for. Resigning takes one sheet of paper.

chapters.title: Status Games You Didn't Enter
chapters.tease: When you walk at 11:47 p.m. just to defend a step count, the ruler has started running you.

chapters.title: The Benchmark Trap, Personal Edition
chapters.tease: Once you ship something, the work is fixed. So why does your mood keep swinging with the numbers?

chapters.title: Kudos Fasting
chapters.tease: There is one rival worth beating, whose footage you own completely and whose defeat harms nobody.

chapters.title: The Only Rival
chapters.tease: An hour of good work that nobody will ever see might be the most honest thing you do all year.

chapters.title: The Unwatched Hour
chapters.tease: A second pair of hands now sits at every desk. The real question is what is still yours to do.

chapters.title: The Second Pair of Hands
chapters.tease: Nobody holds a funeral when a machine absorbs your craft, but something does die, and grieving it is allowed.

chapters.title: Pride of Craft, Grief of Craft
chapters.tease: You have been promoted from maker to chooser. Nobody threw a party, and there is nowhere left to hide.

chapters.title: The Editor Ascends
chapters.tease: The machine makes forty versions before your coffee cools. The whole art now lives in one spoonful and a verdict.

chapters.title: Delegate the Task, Keep the Taste
chapters.tease: The famous centaur chess story is out of date. The posture it describes still matters more than ever.

chapters.title: The Centaur's Posture
chapters.tease: Anyone can generate. Only someone can vouch. Your signature is the one thing the machine cannot produce.

chapters.title: What You Sign
chapters.tease: The machine's disappointing answer can usually be traced, embarrassingly, to the question you gave it.

chapters.title: The Prompt Is a Mirror
chapters.tease: The machines are running, you are standing in the kitchen, and the guilt is entirely misplaced.

chapters.title: Idle Hands, Quiet Mind
chapters.tease: Every correction you give the machine teaches it to need you less. Every master has faced that, and taught anyway.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Never Tires
chapters.tease: Every good workshop keeps one retired tool on the shelf. Which way of working are you ready to put there?

chapters.title: The Laid-Down Tool
chapters.tease: Thirty seconds of buffering now feels like hardship. The patience muscle has wasted away, and it can be rebuilt.

chapters.title: The Collapse of Waiting
chapters.tease: A long human life, counted in weeks, fits in four digits. What on that budget was never worth a cell?

chapters.title: Four Thousand Weeks
chapters.tease: The letter was better than its contents. Friction was quietly editing everything, and then we fired it.

chapters.title: Slow Is a Feature
chapters.tease: One defended hour a day quietly outbuilds every heroic all-nighter. The arithmetic is almost embarrassing.

chapters.title: The Compound Hour
chapters.tease: A man presses a lift button that is already lit. Welcome to hurry sickness, where no second is ever saved.

chapters.title: Hurry Sickness
chapters.tease: The famous line about the space between stimulus and response was never Viktor Frankl's. The space is real anyway.

chapters.title: The Pause Between
chapters.tease: No orchard has ever been persuaded that apples should really happen in Q4. Your work has seasons too.

chapters.title: Seasons, Not Sprints
chapters.tease: The most hated object in working life turns out to be a small philosophical instrument about mortality.

chapters.title: The Deadline as Memento
chapters.tease: The quote about enjoyable wasted time is not Lennon's. It comes from a 1912 novel almost nobody has read.

chapters.title: Time You Enjoyed Wasting
chapters.tease: An hour with nothing in it: no input, no output, no phone. It is the hardest practice in the section.

chapters.title: The Empty Hour
chapters.tease: Opinions used to cost an evening at the library. Now they are printed by the million, and worth about that much.

chapters.title: Opinion Inflation
chapters.tease: The internet's favourite Marcus Aurelius quote is not in the Meditations. The real Marcus is sharper.

chapters.title: “Everything We Hear Is an Opinion”
chapters.tease: The internet says silence concedes. Nobody ever passed that rule, and you never signed it.

chapters.title: The Right to Remain Silent
chapters.tease: Strong views, loosely held, sounds wise. In practice, people rarely get round to the loosening part.

chapters.title: Strong Views, Loosely Held
chapters.tease: There is a small pundit at a small desk inside your head, providing rolling coverage of your life. It can be rescheduled.

chapters.title: The Commentariat of One
chapters.tease: Cutting news helps, but going totally dark is a luxury. Here is the honest middle path, with a single filter.

chapters.title: News Fasting, Honestly
chapters.tease: You are undefeated in the shower. Three thousand wins, no losses, and an audience of precisely nobody.

chapters.title: The Argument You Won in the Shower
chapters.tease: Reading the other side at its strongest is not a virtue. It is armour, and it protects you.

chapters.title: Charity as Armor
chapters.tease: No ethical system ever said strangers are owed unlimited access to your attention. Not even the Stoics.

chapters.title: The Block Button Is Stoic
chapters.tease: The noise did not lose, and it never will. But you can close a door and make your own thought the loudest thing.

chapters.title: The Quiet Room
chapters.tease: It started with a to-do app. Two years later, the system gets fed first and the work gets the leftovers.

chapters.title: The Productivity Ouroboros
chapters.tease: Seneca wrote the greatest essay against busyness while holding one of Rome's largest fortunes. Both facts matter.

chapters.title: Busy Is Not a Virtue
chapters.tease: The hustle preacher on stage is a returning bomber, describing its bullet holes as the secret to success.

chapters.title: The Hustle Gospel
chapters.tease: A day spent reaching inbox zero is a day spent entirely inside other people's requests, beautifully sorted.

chapters.title: Inbox Zero, Mind Full
chapters.tease: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring. That law applies to your soul as well as monetary policy.

chapters.title: The Metric Becomes the Mission
chapters.tease: The Romans thought leisure was the real work and business was the interruption. They even named it that way.

chapters.title: Rest as Insubordination
chapters.tease: You are performing exhaustion for an audience of machines that cannot see it, in an economy that no longer buys it.

chapters.title: The Machine Doesn't Need You Tired
chapters.tease: Systems beat willpower, mostly. But somebody has to build the system, and that somebody needs a grip.

chapters.title: Systems Over Willpower
chapters.tease: You defined enough for what you take in. Now comes the harder line: enough for what you put out.

chapters.title: Enough, Again
chapters.tease: The day ends when you declare it finished, out loud, on purpose. Otherwise it simply trails off with the laptop half shut.

chapters.title: The Finished Day
chapters.tease: The Romans called an actor's mask a persona. It is now printed, quietly, on every business card.

chapters.title: The Personal Brand Is a Mask
chapters.tease: The archer owns the draw and the aim. The wind owns the rest. An archer who is the arrow dies on every gust.

chapters.title: You Are Not Your Output
chapters.tease: A hundred accepted suggestions later, your writing voice is doing things you never decided. Whose sentence is it?

chapters.title: The Ghost in Your Voice
chapters.tease: Authenticity now converts better than polish, so the real is manufactured at scale, with consultants.

chapters.title: Authenticity™
chapters.tease: Steps, streaks, sleep scores and credit ratings sketch a detailed silhouette of you. They cannot contain the one reading them.

chapters.title: The Aggregate Self
chapters.tease: Being unobserved used to be most of life. Now it is a setting you have to choose on purpose.

chapters.title: The Unperformed Self
chapters.tease: You can reinvent yourself by Thursday online. The trouble is the shredder that usually comes with it.

chapters.title: Reinvention Without Erasure
chapters.tease: A version of you is employed online. Has anyone ever checked what it earns, and what it costs?

chapters.title: The Avatar's Salary
chapters.tease: Character is an interface: a promise about behaviour that other people can build on without checking.

chapters.title: Character Is the Interface
chapters.tease: What if there is nothing beneath the mask? Nine practices of inspection suggest that fear is empty.

chapters.title: The Face Beneath
chapters.tease: When plausible content costs almost nothing, it becomes almost everything. Here is how a lighthouse stands in that tide.

chapters.title: The Slop Tide
chapters.tease: Three small words have nearly vanished from meetings, threads and machines. Saying them is now a competitive advantage.

chapters.title: “I Don't Know”
chapters.tease: A language model sounds equally sure about what it knows and what it invented. Your instincts have not caught up.

chapters.title: The Confidence of Machines
chapters.tease: Fact-checkers have budgets, blind spots and authors. Somewhere the chain of checking ends, and you are simply trusting.

chapters.title: Trust, but Verify the Verifier
chapters.tease: Slop is ultra-processed text. It does not poison you, it simply crowds out the meal.

chapters.title: The Epistemic Diet
chapters.tease: The deepfake's second payload is worse than the first: not the fake believed, but every real thing doubted.

chapters.title: The Liar's Dividend
chapters.tease: Old maps said here be dragons at their edges. Generated maps draw imaginary islands with the same firm line.

chapters.title: The Map Is Generated
chapters.tease: You will go to bed most nights not knowing which claims were true. The skill is carrying that without clenching.

chapters.title: The Still Center of Not-Knowing
chapters.tease: What would your loudest opinions be willing to lose? Ask them politely, and watch the numbers correct themselves.

chapters.title: Skin in the Game
chapters.tease: No system will ever light the whole landscape. But a lantern is enough for the next step, and that is all walking needs.

chapters.title: The Lantern, Not the Sun
chapters.tease: Hanlon's razor is not ancient wisdom or Napoleon. It is a 1980 joke book, and it still cuts beautifully.

chapters.title: Hanlon's Razor, Upgraded
chapters.tease: The offence may have been theirs. The invoice, itemised honestly, is addressed to you.

chapters.title: The Anger Invoice
chapters.tease: Engineers never take a crashed server personally. They do take a colleague's curt message personally. Why?

chapters.title: Assume the Server Is Down
chapters.tease: Marcus began each day expecting rudeness and ingratitude. Read in full, it is not misanthropy, it is tenderness.

chapters.title: The Mercy of Low Expectations
chapters.tease: You may know a streamer's day better than your brother's. The warmth is real. It just flows one way.

chapters.title: Parasocial, Para-Stoic
chapters.tease: A phone face-down on the dinner table, silent, still thins the conversation. So stop fighting it with willpower.

chapters.title: The Dinner Table Protocol
chapters.tease: An unforgiven wrong is a background process running on your hardware. The person who caused it is not even logged in.

chapters.title: Forgiveness as Cache-Clearing
chapters.tease: The perfect AI companion never tires, never leaves, never needs anything back. That is exactly what it lacks.

chapters.title: Love in the Agentic Age
chapters.tease: A second-century Stoic drew circles of care from self to species. The internet wired the outer ring straight to your nerves.

chapters.title: The Widening Circle
chapters.tease: After all the infrastructure of this section, the simplest deliverable in the book remains: sit with someone.

chapters.title: The Bench
chapters.tease: Amor fati sounds like ancient Stoic Latin. It was actually coined by Nietzsche in 1882, and the difference matters.

chapters.title: Amor Fati Is Not Ancient
chapters.tease: Pull the camera back far enough and the inbox disappears. Then comes the important part: coming back down.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Zoom
chapters.tease: Mortal creatures, furious about parking on a four-billion-year-old rock. You are not in a tragedy. Check the ticket.

chapters.title: The Joke You're In
chapters.tease: There are two laughs. One builds rooms, the other slowly eats them. The difference is a single preposition.

chapters.title: Laughing With, Not At
chapters.tease: That mortifying blunder will be your best dinner story in ten years. Why wait to release the comedy?

chapters.title: The Comedy of Errors, Yours
chapters.tease: The general's slave probably never whispered memento mori. But death and the laugh turn out to be collaborators.

chapters.title: Memento LOL
chapters.tease: The Serenity Prayer is not ancient. It is a 1930s remix, and you can hear the Stoic sample instantly.

chapters.title: The Serenity Remix
chapters.tease: The infinite scroll from chapter one returns, and it turns out to have an end after all.

chapters.title: The Last Scroll
chapters.tease: The witness's ochre notebook is full. One line remains, and it is the one this book cannot write for you.

chapters.title: The Notebook, Full
chapters.tease: One hundred practices compile to a single word, said sincerely. The mask comes all the way off.
